reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer 2 characterized the investigation of aerosol acidity–concentration interactions as novel and interesting. The final manuscript defines the proposed buffering-driven particulate response and reports the associated multi-method study in P:S-16bdf69001f935ed4c23 and P:S-6a3bf8dc3cad23465ad7.

The reviewer requested clarification of how the Figure 2a construct was synthesized. The final caption identifies it as a conceptual schematic based on common trends across nine events in P:S-e92ca4149929ecb5a4cc; this preserves a mechanism/metric-level novelty boundary rather than a quantitatively aggregated figure claim.

Reviewer 1 identified the long-term observations, global simulations, and machine-learning analysis as complementary elements. The final paper documents the four-year observation and experimental basis in P:S-2afee0202a3252478b55 and the global and driver analyses in P:S-6a3bf8dc3cad23465ad7.

Reviewer 2 highlighted the novel investigation of aerosol acidity and concentration. The final manuscript supplies the response-mechanism account and reports long-term and high-time-resolution observational support in P:S-ef99b8fafa642a565cf0 and P:S-87f19f819a2104b6442b.

The reviewer identified the discrete MF/AF treatment as a methodological limitation because aerosol water and other factors are co-dependent. The final paper explicitly retains this limitation in P:S-7c50cc25a00ec843e13f, stating that absolute contributions may be uncertain and synergy underestimated.

The reviewer requested a reproducible account of Figure 2a construction. P:S-e92ca4149929ecb5a4cc now clearly labels it conceptual and trend-based, but this means the figure is not itself a quantitative aggregation of the nine events.

Reviewer 2 questioned whether four 2019 model months could substantiate interpretation of global spatial patterns. The final paper retains January, April, July, and October 2019 monthly-average GEOS-Chem inputs in P:S-63a99701304a27620182 while making seasonal pattern claims in P:S-0a1875d9f9fb1c7bfb3f.

Audit-only: the request for direct comparison of calculated Co-P with measured particulate ammonium was answered by a reported event-level comparison. P:S-87f19f819a2104b6442b independently confirms that the final paper includes high-time-resolution monitoring to investigate the response mechanism.

Audit-only: the emission-inventory sensitivity and model-resolution concerns were addressed. P:S-eb7989bf829127406ee1 states that inventory spatiotemporal resolution and emission uncertainty are discussed, and P:S-63a99701304a27620182 specifies the 2° × 2.5° model resolution.

Audit-only: the terminology objection was addressed by replacing feedback terminology with response terminology and adding its physical account. P:S-ef99b8fafa642a565cf0 and P:S-87f19f819a2104b6442b provide the final mechanism description.

Audit-only: the request for random-forest hyperparameters and validation was addressed. P:S-111140772faa99c56852 supplies the hyperparameter section and P:S-8be8c68ca953b7950d72 reports ten-fold cross-validation and train/test performance.

limiting_points.suggested_action: State the contribution as a calculated, pH-perturbation-based metric and mechanism, distinct from a directly measured pollutant burden.
limiting_points.text: The contribution is bounded by a calculated concomitant-pollution framework: Figure 2a is a conceptual schematic based on common trends across nine events, rather than a quantitative aggregation of those events.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Preserve the mechanism-level framing that links multiphase buffering, gas-to-particle partitioning, and particulate-mass response.
supporting_points.text: The study advances a novel and interesting mechanism-level account of how aerosol-acidity buffering can alter particle mass through reactive-nitrogen phase partitioning.

questions.suggested_action: Report sensitivity of regional and seasonal conclusions to additional years and submonthly or additional monthly sampling.
questions.text: The global analysis uses monthly-average GEOS-Chem inputs for January, April, July, and October 2019. How robust are the reported seasonal and regional Co-P rankings beyond those four representative months?

strengths.suggested_action: Document the complementary roles of the long-term observations, experiments, global simulation, and driver analysis when presenting the evidence chain.
strengths.text: The evidence chain combines four years of continuous observations and laboratory experiments with global simulation and machine-learning analyses of drivers.

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the linkage between the chemical response mechanism and the long-term and high-time-resolution observational evidence.
strengths.text: The manuscript connects a concrete NH4+/NH3 phase-partitioning response mechanism to long-term observations and added high-time-resolution monitoring evidence.

summary.text: The manuscript examines buffering-driven gas-to-particle conversion of reactive nitrogen as a contributor to concomitant particulate pollution, using long-term observations, experiments, machine-learning driver analysis, and global GEOS-Chem simulations. Its central contribution is a mechanism and calculated Co-P framework linking stable aerosol acidity to changing particulate mass, with global seasonal and regional patterns. The remaining limits concern the conceptual MF/AF attribution and the temporal coverage supporting global pattern interpretation.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Treat MF/AF as a relative diagnostic and quantify the sensitivity of conclusions to interaction-aware attribution approaches.
weaknesses.text: MF/AF remains a conceptual simplification: meteorological and anthropogenic factors are interdependent, so its discrete ratio can leave absolute contributions uncertain and underestimate synergistic effects.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Keep the conceptual status prominent and provide event-level quantities separately where the schematic is used to support interpretation.
weaknesses.text: Figure 2a is explicitly conceptual and based on common event trends; it should not be read as a quantitatively averaged or directly fitted representation of the nine events.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The revision acknowledges the MF/AF limitation, but the interdependence and potential synergy of its factor classes remain a limit on absolute attribution.
The figure's construction is clarified, while its conceptual and non-aggregated character remains relevant to interpretation.
Specific climate-mode assertions were removed, but the global patterns continue to rest on four representative 2019 monthly simulations.
The response reports an event-level Co-P versus particulate-ammonium comparison and correlation; this item is audit-only.
The final paper states the inventory-uncertainty treatment and the GEOS-Chem resolution; this item is audit-only.
Hyperparameters and cross-validation are supplied in the final paper; this item is audit-only.
